verdict: key consistent: 87 signs = 87 letters of the verse as the cipher has it, 23 groups = 23 words; one letter per shape; ا has three shapes (S1; S8 once; S24 once, brown ink), ل two (S9; S6 once in على), ف two (S21, S22); S7 = ي and the ئ seat of لامرئ
notes: Rows: 9v segmenter lines 2-9 (8 rows; the record gives 7 rows and lines 3-10). Segmenter line 2's box covers only the left part; the row runs from the right margin under 'ومنها' (اصبر على = signs 1-7). Measured 12+12+11+11+11+12+13+5 = 87 signs (record 83) and 23 dividers (record 16). Record errors: (1) the cipher includes the interlinear القدر after تشتهي (9v.5 end + 9v.6 first sign: S1 S9 S10 S11 S4, the same spelling as القدر in 9v.2), so it is part of the enciphered verse; (2) the cipher has سيتبع (5 signs S23 S7 S14 S3 S5) and صفوه (S2 S22 S15 S17, S17 = ه as in به and تشتهي), not سيتبعه ... صفو: the pronoun sits on صفو (الا سيتبع يوما صفوه الكدر); (3) the 'lam-alif-like sign' on the last row is two signs written touching: S19 (ك, as in اتاك) and S11 (د, as in القدر), z_r9lam.png; الكدر is spelled out in 5 signs. With these, the dividers follow the words (23 groups = 23 words with القدر added; the record's '17 groups vs 22 words' is a miscount). Doubtful: 9v.7 الا has its first ا as a plain stroke in brown ink (S24) over the line, a later addition; without it the cipher wrote لا. A brown cup sign under 9v.6 (between S1 and S12 of لامر) and a small mark over S17 in 9v.7 are not counted. S8 (ا of the first القدر) looks very like S4 (ر); if merged S4 would read ر 5 / ا 1. لامرئ: the hamza seat is written with S7 (ي), counted as ئ.
